name: Shaving
overview: Scripture addresses shaving in various contexts, emphasizing its significance in holiness and separation to the Lord. Nazarites are commanded not to let a razor touch their heads during their vow, symbolizing their dedication (Numbers 6:5), and only shave their heads at the completion of their separation (Numbers 6:18). Priests are instructed to avoid shaving the corners of their heads and beards, maintaining distinctiveness and reverence (Leviticus 19:27; 21:5). Additionally, shaving the body is associated with ceremonial cleansing (Numbers 8:7), while Joseph’s shaving before meeting Pharaoh (Genesis 41:14) reflects personal preparation and respect. These verses collectively show that shaving was not merely a cultural practice but carried spiritual and covenantal meaning in the Old Testament.
